extracted.intended_audience: graduate students (or advanced undergraduates) studying algebraic geometry; readers of Vakil's The Rising Sea
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the key definitions, theorems, and conditions from a textbook excerpt covering Serre duality on P1, classification of vector bundles on P1, Hilbert functions/polynomials, degree/genus, B´ezout, higher direct images, base change, projection formula, relative vanishing, and Serre's cohomological ampleness criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre duality pairing on P1
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a natural perfect pairing H0(P1, O(n)) × H1(P1, O(−2 − n)) → k (for P1_k). For n > 0, H0 corresponds to homogeneous degree n polynomials and H1 to certain Laurent polynomials; pairing is given by multiplication and reading off the coefficient of x^{−1}y^{−1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works more generally for P^n_A (discussion after Theorem 18.1.2). The text explains how to interpret factors for n<0 (both factors 0) and gives the concrete recipe (multiply, get degree −2 Laurent polynomial, read x^{-1}y^{-1}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ample divisors on connected smooth projective varieties are connected (exercise 18.5.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming Serre duality: If X is a connected smooth projective k-variety of dimension ≥ 2 and D is an effective ample divisor, then D is connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint/sketch: write D = V(s) for a section s of an ample invertible sheaf L, replace L by a high power so V(sn)=V(s), use the long exact sequence for 0 → OX(−nD) → OX → O_{V(sn)} → 0 to deduce h^0(X,O_{V(sn)}) = 1. Note extensions to Cohen–Macaulay projective schemes once Serre duality is available there; counterexamples exist when X is not Cohen–Macaulay (e.g., union of two 2-planes in P^4 meeting at a point).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of vector bundles on P1 (Grothendieck's Theorem, Theorem 18.5.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If E is a rank r vector bundle on P1_k, then E ≅ O(a1) ⊕ ··· ⊕ O(ar) for a unique nondecreasing sequence of integers a1 ≤ ··· ≤ ar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness can be recovered from dims of Hom(O(m),E) (Exercise 18.5.C). The proof uses cohomology (induction on rank, choose maximal ar with Hom(O(ar),E)≠0, show injection, cokernel locally free, continue). Historical notes: proved many times (Grothendieck, Dedekind–Weber), generalizations (Horrocks criterion) fail in higher dimension without additional hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinability of splitting types from Hom dimensions (Exercise 18.5.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The integers a_i in the splitting E ≅ ⊕ O(a_i) can be determined from the numbers dim_k Hom(O(m), E) as m ranges over Z; this yields uniqueness of the decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Hom(O(m),E) ≅ H^0(P1, E(−m)) (Exercise 14.2.G) and analyze dimensions as functions of m.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert function is eventually polynomial (Theorem 18.6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a coherent sheaf F on a projective k-scheme X ⊂ P^n_k, the Euler characteristic χ(X, F(m)) is a polynomial in m of degree equal to dim Supp F, and for m ≫ 0, h^0(X, F(m)) equals this polynomial p_F(m). In particular, h^0(X, O_X(m)) is polynomial of degree dim X for large m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: reduce to algebraically closed infinite k, choose hyperplane missing associated points to reduce dimension (short exact sequence 0 → F(−1) → F → G → 0), use additivity of Euler characteristic to induct on dimension. Serre vanishing gives equality of h^0 and χ for large m.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Hilbert polynomial (Definition 18.6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For coherent F on projective scheme X, define p_F(m) := χ(X, F(m)). For X ⊂ P^n_k, p_X(m) := p_{O_X}(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions: degree of zero polynomial and dimension of empty set are −1; only the zero-sheaf has Hilbert polynomial 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational formulas for Hilbert polynomials of standard embeddings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: p_{P^n}(m) = (m + n choose n). If H ⊂ P^n is a degree d hypersurface, then p_H(m) = p_{P^n}(m) − p_{P^n}(m − d). Twisted cubic in P^3 (image of P^1 by |O(3)|) has Hilbert polynomial 3m + 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use closed subscheme exact sequence 0 → O_{P^n}(−d) → O_{P^n} → O_H → 0 and projection formula / transition-function calculations where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree and arithmetic genus from Hilbert polynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: For a projective k-scheme X of dimension n, deg(X) is the leading coefficient of p_X(m) times n!. The arithmetic genus is (−1)^n (χ(X, O_X) − 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: deg(P^n)=1, twisted cubic has degree 3; plugging m=0 into p_X yields χ(O_X) which is intrinsic (independent of embedding). Use Riemann–Roch for curves to relate degree of line bundle and degree of embedding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integers nature of degree (Exercise 18.6.F)
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree of a projective scheme is always an integer: if a polynomial f of degree k takes integer values at all integers, the leading coefficient is an integral multiple of 1/k!.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove by induction using finite differences: f(x+1) − f(x) has integer values and degree k−1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert polynomial detects equality of embedded subschemes (Exercise 18.6.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If X ⊂ Y ⊂ P^n_k are closed embeddings, then p_X(m) ≤ p_Y(m) for m ≫ 0. (b) If p_X(m) = p_Y(m) for m ≫ 0, then X = Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exact sequence 0 → I_{X/Y}(m) → O_Y(m) → O_X(m) → 0 and the fact that if Hilbert polynomial of a coherent sheaf is 0 then the sheaf is 0; apply to I_{X/Y}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bézout's theorem and degree of intersections (18.6.4 and Exercise 18.6.J/M)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X ⊂ P^n_k and H is a hypersurface not containing any associated points of X, then deg(H ∩ X) = (deg H)(deg X). For plane curves of degrees m and n with no common components, they meet in mn points counted with multiplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires control of associated points (e.g., reduced curves have none). Multiplicity of intersection interpreted as degree of intersection scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of complete intersections (18.6.9 and related exercises)
rubrics_metrics.description: A codimension-r complete intersection in P^n_k is cut out by r hypersurfaces and has pure codimension r. For such X of dimension m, one often has h^i(X, O_X(n)) = 0 for 0 < i < m (Exercise 18.6.Q). Complete intersections of positive dimension are connected (Exercise 18.6.U).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/exercises: genus computations for complete intersections in P^3 (18.6.R, 18.6.S), rational normal curve is not a complete intersection for d>2 (18.6.T), degree additivity for unions with no common top-dimensional components (18.6.O). Use Krull's Height Theorem for codimension assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher direct image (pushforward) sheaves—definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For π : X → Y quasicompact and separated and F a quasicoherent sheaf on X, define the sheaf R^i π_* F on Y by assigning to Spec A ⊂ Y the A-module H^i(π^{-1}(Spec A), F); these patch to a quasicoherent sheaf because cohomology commutes with localization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computation via Čech complexes and localization (FHHF exercise). Caution: for a general open U ⊂ Y, H^0(U, R^•π_* F) need not equal H^•(π^{-1}(U), F) except for affine U.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic properties of higher pushforwards (Theorem 18.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) R^i π_* : QCoh_X → QCoh_Y is a covariant functor. (b) R^0 π_* = π_*. (c) A short exact sequence 0 → F → G → H → 0 on X induces a long exact sequence of sheaves 0 → R^0π_*F → R^0π_*G → R^0π_*H → R^1π_*F → ···. (d) (Grothendieck's coherence theorem) If π is projective, O_Y coherent, and F coherent on X, then for all i, R^iπ_*F is coherent on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All parts can be checked on affine opens of Y using Čech cohomology; (d) is the coherence theorem for projective morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine morphism vanishing (Easy exercise 18.7.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π is affine, then for i > 0, R^i π_* F = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is immediate from vanishing of higher cohomology on affine schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base change and push-pull map for higher pushforwards (Exercise 18.7.B & 18.7.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a Cartesian square with ψ : Y' → Y and corresponding π', there is a natural morphism ψ^*(R^iπ_* F) → R^iπ'_* (ψ')^* F. For affine flat/flat base change this map is an isomorphism; more generally there is a natural map from the fiber (R^iπ_*F) ⊗ κ(q) to H^i(π^{-1}(q), F|_{π^{-1}(q)}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FHHF and flatness/affineness hypotheses to get isomorphisms (cohomology commutes with flat base change). The fiber map need not be an iso in general but will be in 'good' situations (Cohomology and Base Change Theorem 26.1.6 later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Projection formula for higher pushforwards (Exercise 18.7.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π : X → Y quasicompact & separated and quasicoherent F on X, G on Y, there is a natural morphism (R^iπ_* F) ⊗ G → R^iπ_*(F ⊗ π^*G), which is an isomorphism when G is locally free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct via FHHF; use locally free hypothesis to interchange tensor and higher direct image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative dimensional cohomology vanishing (Theorem 18.7.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a projective morphism and Y is locally Noetherian (or O_Y coherent), then R^iπ_*F = 0 for i greater than the maximum dimension of the fibers of π.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False without projectivity (example: open embedding A^n \\ {0} → A^n). Proof: reduce locally on Y, cover fiber by m+1 affines to force vanishing above m via affine cover cohomology vanishing; hence R^iπ_*F vanishes near point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Serre vanishing (Exercise 18.7.F)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is proper with Y Noetherian and L is π-ample invertible on X, then for any coherent F on X there exists m0 such that for m ≥ m0, R^iπ_*(F ⊗ L^{⊗ m}) = 0 for all i > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analog of Serre vanishing in relative/projective families; used to show cohomology vanishing in high twists in families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre's cohomological criterion for ampleness (Theorem 18.8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be Noetherian, X a proper A-scheme, and L an invertible sheaf on X. Then L is ample on X (over A) iff for all coherent sheaves F on X there exists n_0 such that for n ≥ n_0, H^i(X, F ⊗ L^{⊗ n}) = 0 for all i > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theorem lists equivalent conditions (a–c) and the cohomological criterion (e). The section is starred (not used later) but gives a cohomological characterization of ampleness under Noetherian hypotheses.
